workflow.purpose:
Create or update a guide document in `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/guides/`.
A guide is a step-by-step recipe for a common implementation task. It combines knowledge from multiple systems, patterns, and cross-cutting concerns into one actionable recipe. The document an AI agent follows when performing a recurring task end-to-end.
This workflow is executed directly — NO sub-agents are spawned. The executing agent does everything: finding reference implementations, reading code, deriving the recipe, and writing the document.
workflow.mandatory-context: Read all files referenced by the invoking command's execution-context before starting. Also read any document or text passed as parameter ($ARGUMENTS) in the invoking command.

process.step:
Display stage banner:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map Guide ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ```
Parse $ARGUMENTS for: `text`, `subsystem`, `story-context`, `commits`.
**If `text` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "Guide" - question: "Describe the recurring task this guide should teach.\nE.g., 'How to add a new drawing tool' or 'How to add a new CRUD endpoint'"
**If `subsystem` is missing:** Ask the user: - header: "Guide" - question: "Which subsystem does this guide belong to?"
Resolve the subsystem. Check if `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem-name]/` exists.
**If not found:** ``` ! No wiki found for subsystem "[subsystem]". Run /ace:map-subsystem first to create the subsystem wiki. ``` Exit.
Ensure guides directory exists: ```bash mkdir -p .docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/guides ```
Display: ``` i Guide: [text description] Subsystem: [subsystem-name] Story context: [path/issue, or "none"] Commits: [value, or "search codebase directly"] ```
Continue to step 2.

Scan for existing guides:
``` Glob(pattern='*.md', path='.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/guides') ```
**If existing guides found:** Read their titles. Check if any covers the same or overlapping task.
**If overlap detected:** Use AskUserQuestion: - header: "Guide" - question: "An existing guide may cover a similar task:\n\n- `[existing-file]`: [title]\n\nShould I update the existing guide or create a new one?" - options: - "Update existing" — set MODE = update, set TARGET_FILE = existing path - "Create new" — set MODE = create
**If no overlap or no existing guides:** Set MODE = create.
**If MODE = create:** Derive file name from task description in kebab-case (e.g., "how-to-add-drawing-tool.md"). Set TARGET_FILE = `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/guides/[guide-name].md`
Continue to step 3.

Read all markdown files in the story artifacts folder. Extract: what was built, which files were touched, which registrations were added.
```bash gh issue view [issue-number] --json title,body,labels,comments ``` Extract context about the task and implementation.
Skip — derive recipe from codebase patterns only.
```bash git diff --name-only HEAD~[N]..HEAD ``` Filter to files within the subsystem. These are the most recent example. Read each file to understand the implementation steps taken.
```bash git diff --name-only [first-sha]^..[last-sha] ``` Filter to files within the subsystem. Read each file.
Use the `text` description to find existing implementations of this task:
1. Read the subsystem's structure.md and architecture.md for orientation 2. Read existing system/pattern/cross-cutting docs for this subsystem 3. Grep for keywords related to the task (class names, registrations, etc.) 4. Find 2-3 existing implementations that followed the same recipe 5. Read each implementation to extract the common steps
From the reference implementations, derive the step-by-step recipe:
1. What files need to be created? In what order? 2. What existing files need to be modified (registrations, configurations)? 3. What patterns must be followed (from patterns/ docs)? 4. What cross-cutting registrations are needed (from cross-cutting/ docs)? 5. What is the closest existing implementation to copy from? 6. What commonly goes wrong?
Build an ordered list of steps with "copy from" references.
Continue to step 4.

Read ALL existing wiki docs under `.docs/wiki/subsystems/[subsystem_name]/` for cross-referencing in Prerequisites and linking to patterns/systems.
Follow the guide template structure exactly.
- Title: "# How to [Task]" - Prerequisites: links to pattern docs, system docs, cross-cutting docs that an agent should read BEFORE starting
Write NUMBERED, ORDERED steps. Each step must have: - WHAT to do - WHERE to do it (exact file path) - WHAT to copy from (reference implementation) - Key changes from the reference
Include ALL steps: file creation, registration, configuration, wiring. Don't skip "obvious" steps — agents don't infer implicit requirements.
Write a verification checklist: - Compilation check - Runtime check - Behavioral check Reference specific files or commands.
List things that commonly go wrong: - WHY each mistake happens - HOW to avoid it Drawn from actual gotchas in pattern/system docs and codebase analysis.
**If MODE = create:** Write the complete document to TARGET_FILE. **If MODE = update:** Read the existing guide, update steps, add new mistakes, update "copy from" references. Write to TARGET_FILE.
Continue to step 5.

Re-read TARGET_FILE and verify:
Title follows "# How to [Task]" format Prerequisites section links to relevant docs Steps are NUMBERED and ORDERED Every step has WHAT, WHERE, and WHAT to copy from All registrations and configurations included (no implicit steps) Verification checklist present with compilation, runtime, behavioral checks Common Mistakes section present with WHY and HOW Code references use `file:Symbol` format, not line numbers No filler phrases, no generic advice An agent could follow this guide end-to-end without guessing
Fix any failures by editing the document directly.
``` Grep( pattern="(sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}|sk_live_|sk_test_|ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}|AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}|-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY)", path="[TARGET_FILE]", output_mode="content" ) ```
SECRETS_FOUND — alert user, do NOT commit. CLEAN.
```bash git add [TARGET_FILE] git commit -m "docs([subsystem_name]): add guide — [guide-name]" ```
Display:
``` ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ ACE > Map Guide > Complete ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
+ [TARGET_FILE] ([line count] lines)
Guide: [text description] Steps: [step count] Prerequisites: [count] docs linked Common Mistakes: [count]
Next > /clear first for a fresh context window, then:
/ace:map-guide — create another guide /ace:map-pattern — document a pattern referenced by this guide /ace:map-sys-doc — document a system referenced by this guide Review file at [TARGET_FILE] ```
End workflow.

success_criteria.criterion: Task description parsed and subsystem validated
Reference implementations found (from commits or codebase search)
Recipe derived from actual code — not invented from generic knowledge
Existing guides checked to avoid duplication (create vs update decision)
Guide follows template structure from guide.xml
Prerequisites link to relevant pattern/system/cross-cutting docs
Steps are numbered, ordered, and each has WHAT/WHERE/copy-from
ALL steps included — no implicit requirements
Verification checklist covers compilation, runtime, and behavior
Common Mistakes section includes WHY and HOW for each
Code references use file:Symbol format, no line numbers
No filler, no generic advice, no pseudocode
